outcome: A single security standard protects municipal data and network infrastructure across every building and service in the estate.
overview: Abu Dhabi City Municipality deployed Fortinet security to protect critical municipal data and networks — a published reference on the vendor’s own site, and the clearest kind of proof point a distributor can carry into a public-sector conversation. Municipal estates are awkward in a specific way: many services, many buildings, several networks that grew separately, and a public expectation that none of it stops. The Security Fabric approach suits that shape — one policy and logging model across a heterogeneous estate rather than a device-by-device rebuild.

benefits.text: One policy and logging model spans a municipal estate built by separate projects
benefits.limits: The published reference describes one named customer engagement. It is evidence that Redington has delivered this, and it is not a performance figure that transfers to the next customer

benefits.text: Security telemetry from across the estate is readable in one place
benefits.limits: Fabric integration is deepest between the same vendor’s components; third-party devices integrate through standard interfaces with less context

benefits.text: New buildings and services can be added to an existing standard rather than designed afresh
benefits.limits: The same operating system runs on the appliance, as a virtual machine and in cloud, so the capability claim survives a form-factor change; the throughput figure behind it does not, and must be re-sized per form factor

residency: Devices, management and logs remain inside the entity’s own estate, which is the required position for municipal data in this jurisdiction

notFor.situation: An entity already standardised on another vendor’s integrated security platform
notFor.why: Fabric value comes from integration depth, and a mixed estate gets the interfaces without the depth

notFor.situation: A single-service department with one network and one boundary
notFor.why: There is no heterogeneity to unify, and a single boundary does not need a fabric

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet implementation partner · Duration: 16–24 weeks for a first tranche; estate-wide programmes run to the entity’s own phasing
Support model: Vendor hardware and subscription support with a replacement term appropriate to municipal service criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case.
1) Review — building and service inventory, existing device estate, retention obligations per service
2) Define — the estate security standard, central policy model and the phasing plan
3) Deploy — first tranche of buildings and services brought onto the standard
4) Extend and hand over — remaining tranches on the phasing plan, operations handed over
deliverables: A new building can be brought onto the standard from the central policy without a bespoke design
An event spanning two services is visible as one in the estate log store
Each service’s log retention matches its stated criticality
effort: 16–24 weeks for a first tranche; estate-wide programmes run to the entity’s own phasing
